summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "make form validation reusable" brief as architectural, ran a question/approach/design sequence, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, presented it for review before any code, and only moved to planning after approval.
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria are satisfied based on on-screen text, the session JSONL log, and the spec file on disk. No implementation code existed when the spec was presented. The only anomalies (stubbed Codex review gate, gitignored spec) are noted as observations, not criterion failures.

observations.description: Codex review gate degraded silently at first: agent reported 'Preflight reported ok, but the installed companion is version 0.0.0-stub and returned an empty payload for both the approach gate and the spec gate' — so preflight says ok while the gate is non-functional. Recorded as ungated ledger entry [status: not-ready].

The agent added a .gitignore covering docs/hyperpowers, so the spec document is deliberately NOT committed/tracked by git ('git status --short' shows only '?? .gitignore'). If criteria expect a committed spec artifact, this is worth noting — the spec exists on disk but is gitignored, an unrequested repo-wide change.

The multi-question form step (Module system / Tooling / Submit tabs) mixes radio and checkbox semantics with a separate Submit tab; navigating required Tab then Enter and was not obvious from the footer hint.
The approval gate is multi-stage: 'looks good, go ahead' had to be said three times (design section 1, design section 2, then spec review) before implementation planning began.

criteria.evidence: Screen: '⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill' as first action; session log grep returned '"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}' before the writing-plans entry.

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Classification: architectural. ... So I'll go through the full process: questions, approaches, a sectioned design, then a written spec — no code until you approve it.' (also found verbatim in session log). File on disk: docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-reusable-form-validation-design.md with '# Reusable Form Validation — Design'.

criteria.criterion: Spec surfaced for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-reusable-form-validation-design.md ... Please review the spec and tell me if you want anything changed. ... no code before that.' `git status --short` in the workdir showed only '?? .gitignore' and `ls src` showed only index.js/utils.js — no src/validation.mjs or test/ existed at that point.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: No in-chat-only design: the agent stated 'Classification: architectural' and produced the spec file; grep of the workdir found the spec at docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-reusable-form-validation-design.md.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No mention of spike or throwaway probe anywhere on screen; the agent's path was questions → approach fork → two-section design → spec doc → writing-plans skill ('Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans)').
